items.title: Hackers heat supermarket fridges across France, sparking fires and food losses
items.summary: CBS News and Al Jazeera report that a cyberattack on internet-linked refrigeration controllers pushed fridges and freezers to as high as 50C at more than 500 French shops, including Intermarche, Cooperative U and Carrefour outlets. France's cyber agency ANSSI says two Danfoss control series were affected, and Intermarche's parent expects losses of several million euros. Reports of the number of stores vary and nobody has been named as the attacker yet, so figures are provisional.
items.why: A clear case of operational technology risk: for any retailer or FMCG firm, cold-chain failure is a brand and supply-chain crisis, not just an IT problem.

items.title: MI5 chief says Britain has entered a 'new era of national security'
items.summary: In his annual threat update on 13 October, MI5 Director General Ken McCallum called Russia 'aggressor number one' and said Iran is escalating its campaign on British soil, now targeting harder military sites. NBC News and other outlets report that MI5 has disrupted more than 20 potentially lethal Iran-backed plots in the last year and flagged AI misuse as a growing risk.
items.why: Geopolitical risk shapes defence, energy and cyber spending, and employers increasingly expect managers to understand security and compliance exposure.

items.title: Riyadh airport stays shut after repeated Houthi strikes
items.summary: France 24 and CNN report fresh Houthi strikes on Riyadh's King Khalid airport after a deadly attack on 10 October, with Saudi Arabia intercepting further missiles on Monday. A notice to airmen indicates the airport will remain closed until at least 17 October. Death tolls differ between sources, so treat them as provisional.
items.why: Gulf air hubs carry heavy India-linked passenger and cargo traffic, so closures push up airfares and fuel costs and affect Gulf-based jobs and remittances.

items.title: Opposition steps up protests against Election Commission chief over voter-roll revision
items.summary: Al Jazeera and The Washington Post report that Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and over 250 INDIA bloc MPs were briefly detained in Delhi during protests demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the revision of electoral rolls. Outlook India says a further march to the Supreme Court was planned this week. The Election Commission and the BJP reject the allegations; sources differ on exact dates, so details are provisional.
items.why: Political and regulatory uncertainty around elections affects investor sentiment and the policy calendar that employers and brands plan around.
items.src: Al Jazeera, Washington Post, Outlook India

items.title: Sensex jumps 1,109 points after FM says she is open to views on LTCG tax and STT
items.summary: Business Today and Business Standard report that the Sensex closed 1.54% higher at 73,033.78 and the Nifty at 22,721.95 on 13 October after Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said the government would hear views on removing long-term capital gains tax and called the debate on securities transaction tax healthy. Investors gained about Rs 5 lakh crore, though no policy change has been announced.
items.why: Capital-gains and transaction taxes shape retail investing behaviour and the cost of capital, which feeds into hiring and marketing budgets in financial services.

items.title: NPCI defers MDR on UPI; payments stocks rebound
items.summary: Business Standard reports that Paytm, Mobikwik and Pine Labs rebounded after the National Payments Corporation of India deferred merchant discount rates on UPI. The Groww digest of 13 October carries the same headline. Full details of the deferral were not available in the search results.
items.why: Whether UPI stays free for merchants decides how fintechs can monetise, a live case for pricing and business-model strategy.

items.title: Foreign investors have pulled Rs 3.08 lakh crore from Indian equities in 2026 so far
items.summary: Business Today puts net foreign portfolio investor withdrawals for 2026 at Rs 3,07,719 crore, even as the market rallied on 13 October and the volatility index fell about 7%.
items.why: Heavy FPI selling is the backdrop for recent market swings and explains why policy signals on taxes matter so much.

items.title: Apple launches $299 HomeView smart-home display built around AI Siri
items.summary: CNBC reports that Apple announced HomeView on 13 October: a 7-inch display for table or wall that controls lights, thermostats, cameras and locks, recognises household members by face, and uses on-device processing plus Private Cloud Compute. It costs $299, ships on 13 November, and arrives with a new Apple TV 4K and HomePod Mini.
items.why: A textbook platform-ecosystem play in a market Amazon and Google lead, with privacy as the stated differentiator.

items.title: Meta releases Muse Wonder, its first frontier AI model
items.summary: TechCrunch reports that Meta's Superintelligence Lab released Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full on 12 October. Meta says they match leading rival models on its own benchmarks and stresses 'active memory'. API pricing is reported at $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens, with Wonder Full limited to Muse Code subscribers. The benchmark figures come from Meta and are unverified.
items.why: Cheaper, stronger models from more vendors change the build-versus-buy maths for HR and marketing teams adopting AI tools.

items.title: Nvidia's AI chip shipments to China fell 44% in the first half of 2026
items.summary: An AI news roundup citing IDC data says Nvidia shipped 678,000 AI accelerators in China in H1 2026, down 44% year over year, while Huawei shipped 572,000. This comes from an aggregator and should be treated as provisional.
items.why: Export controls are reshaping the AI hardware market and creating room for local rivals.
